name: Arcturus Defense Solutions HMR-9 'Colossus'
description:
The HMR-9 'Colossus' is a two-handed shock maul developed by Arcturus Defense Solutions for riot suppression, anti-materiel interdiction, and hardened-target neutralization. At 1.4 meters in length and weighing 7.2 kilograms, the Colossus is built around a tungsten-alloy striking head housing a quad-cell capacitor bank capable of storing up to 800,000 volts. A single full-charge strike against a human target delivers neuromuscular incapacitation severe enough to be indistinguishable from cardiac arrest; against light vehicles, the discharge is sufficient to fuse ignition systems, detonate fuel cell regulators, and permanently disable onboard electronics through induced voltage spikes.

The HMR-9 was originally fielded by Arcturus's own internal enforcement divisions for use against fortified Tier 1 barricades and armored vehicles during the 2194 Shelf Uprising, where standard shock batons proved ineffective against crowds using salvaged construction exo-frames. Field reports from that deployment noted that a single Colossus strike to the chassis of a jury-rigged personnel carrier caused total drive failure and secondary electrical fire. Arcturus subsequently made the HMR-9 available to licensed municipal enforcement contractors with appropriate use-of-force documentation.

The weapon has attracted sustained criticism from civil rights organizations, who argue that the 'less-lethal' designation is functionally inaccurate — documented fatality rates in individuals with cardiac implants, BCI systems, or sub-dermal chrome reach approximately 23% per full-charge strike. Arcturus's official position is that the HMR-9 is 'operator-calibrated' and that full-charge deployment against augmented individuals requires supervisor authorization under their published use-of-force protocols, a policy enforcement advocates describe as 'unverifiable in the field.'
legality: Licensed — heavy-discharge maul; requires municipal enforcement contract or licensed security certification; private ownership prohibited in most Meridian districts
specifications:
Length: 1.4 m
Weight: 7.2 kg
Discharge Voltage: Up to 800,000 V (adjustable: 200kV / 500kV / 800kV)
Capacitor Recharge Time: 4 seconds (full charge)
Continuous Strike Mode: 12 consecutive low-charge strikes before recharge required
Battery Life: 40 full-charge strikes per power cell
Power Cell: ADS ProCell-8 (proprietary)
Strike Head Material: Tungsten-carbide composite
Grip: Two-hand insulated polymer, anti-vibration dampening
Anti-Vehicle Rating: Light vehicle electronics, fuel cell regulators
Operating Temperature: -30°C to +65°C
tactical_use: The Colossus is typically deployed by two-person enforcement teams — one operator wielding the maul, one providing cover or crowd management. In vehicle interdiction, a single overhead strike to the hood or door panel of a civilian transport is sufficient to trigger cascading electrical failure. Against personnel, operators are trained to use low-charge settings for standard crowd suppression and reserve full-charge for armored or exo-frame-equipped targets. The weight and swing arc require training; an untrained user risks overextension, making it a poor improvised weapon despite its fearsome reputation.
cultural_context: On the Shelf, the Colossus is called 'Big Blue' — the color of the arc discharge at full charge. It carries a specific dread reputation distinct from ordinary batons; being hit by a standard baton is a common enough experience in Tier 1 that it barely registers as noteworthy, but 'they called in a Big Blue' signals a qualitatively different level of force. Among enforcement personnel, carrying one is a status marker — it means your unit is rated for anti-vehicle ops. Activists have taken to documenting every deployment with the phrase 'Colossus on the ground' as a live alert signal on encrypted mesh boards.
known_users: private industrial security at high-value infrastructure sites
story_hooks: A Colossus-wielding enforcement officer is found dead in a Tier 1 access tunnel — the maul's discharge log shows it was fired seventeen times in ninety seconds, far beyond any standard engagement, and the last strike was directed upward at a drainage grate leading to a Tier 3 residential block.
